_meta.purpose: Provenanced OUTCOME evidence for resolving the pre-committed corridor calibration points in data/calibration-ledger.json. Keyed by target zone. This file records what HAPPENED (did a new lab-confirmed BDBV case appear in the target zone within a point's [pinned_at, resolves_at] window) and is read by calibration_resolver.py. It is deliberately separate from the model snapshot (data/live-bdbv-2026-output.json): Uganda targets are resolved from Uganda MoH / WHO / Africa CDC surveillance, DRC targets from promoted DRC MoH zone-attributed counts. This file never alters the immutable ledger.
doctrine: Importation counts. The corridor predictions are importation/spillover predictions ('a case APPEARS in the target'), so an imported or travel-linked case confirmed in the target zone satisfies the criterion (Kraemer 2019; Klamser 2023).

In-window only. Only a confirmation dated within [pinned_at, resolves_at] resolves a point YES. Pre-window cases (e.g. the 15-16 May Kampala imports) do not count; calibration_resolver.py re-checks the date against each point's window.
Missing entry != NO. A target with no entry here is scored unscoreable_no_feed, never resolved_no.
Provenance required. Every entry cites a source_id and source_url; classification records whether the evidence is resolution-eligible.

Zone attribution for DRC targets. A DRC target resolves on promoted DRC MoH zone-attributed counts: a case counts in the health zone, and from the data date, of the first promoted SitRep that counts it there, even when its sample was taken or tested in the target and even if a later SitRep re-attributes it. For DRC targets this governs over 'Importation counts' (founder ruling 2026-09-26, first applied to kisangani-cod).

Supersede, never edit. A corrected entry is a new dated entry whose supersedes field names the source_id it replaces for the same target zone. The replaced entry stays as written, and calibration_resolver.py reads only the entries no other entry supersedes; two live entries for one target zone are an error.

_meta.retrieval_note: Uganda evidence rechecked 2026-06-20 via the Uganda MoH EVD dashboard API (https://evd-daily.health.go.ug/api/stats): cumulative cases remained 19 with zero new daily cases on 2026-06-18, 2026-06-19, and 2026-06-20. DRC target evidence is refreshed from reviewed INSP SitRep promotions through SitRep #035; Beni first appears in the reviewed SitRep #019 promotion dated 2026-06-02. | 2026-09-01 extension: three targets added that had no entry and were therefore scored unscoreable_no_feed, leaving Blocks 3 and 4 unresolved past their resolution dates (2026-06-25 and 2026-07-04). goma-cod resolved NO from the dated public-ledger resolution; kisangani-cod resolved YES on a 2026-06-30 first confirmation inside its window; yei-ssd resolved NO because South Sudan has reported no confirmed case in this outbreak (WHO DON613 17 July 2026; ECDC page updated 2026-08-31). Two entries carry an explicit residual_uncertainty field. | 2026-09-17 recheck for calibration Block 5 (window 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-01; interim, NOT a resolution): ECDC outbreak page (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda, last updated 2026-09-15) reports Uganda's total as 20 cases between May and June 2026, WHO's end-of-outbreak declaration on 25 August, and no confirmed case in South Sudan; WHO Disease Outbreak News 2026-DON616 (28 August 2026, data to 26 August) lists DRC, Uganda, France and Germany and names South Sudan only as an importation concern. The Uganda MoH EVD dashboard API (https://evd-daily.health.go.ug/api/stats) was re-queried 2026-09-17: 20 cumulative cases, last non-zero day 2026-06-21, series ends 2026-07-28, so it no longer covers the Block 5 window and is not relied on for it. No in-window confirmation exists for arua-uga, bundibugyo-uga, kampala-uga, kasese-uga, nebbi-uga or yei-ssd through 2026-09-15. as_of is set to the newest evidence date (2026-09-15), not the retrieval date, so these points stay pending and cannot resolve NO until the feed is refreshed on or after 2026-10-01. | 2026-09-26 review (founder ruling, dated and documented): kisangani-cod is re-read on promoted DRC MoH zone-attributed counts. INSP SitReps 47, 54, 57 and 58 show no laboratory-confirmed case attributed to a Kisangani health zone between 2026-06-04 and 2026-07-04; the Kisangani health zones first count on 2026-07-11. The new entry insp-zone-attribution-kisangani-2026-09-26 supersedes kisangani-first-confirmation-2026-06-30, which stays in this file as written. as_of is unchanged.

evidence.primary_publisher: Uganda Ministry of Health (announcement, 2026-05-23, as reported)
evidence.pre_window_cases: Two imported Kampala cases confirmed 15 + 16 May 2026 (WHO DON602) are PRE-window and excluded.
evidence.note: On 2026-05-23 Uganda announced 3 new confirmed cases (total 5): the driver who transported the first patient, a health worker, and a woman who travelled DRC->Arua->Entebbe and tested positive at a private hospital in Kampala. >=1 new lab-confirmed case appeared in Kampala within the 20 May-19 June window.

No lab-confirmed case reported in Bundibugyo District (Uganda) through the 2026-06-20 Uganda MoH dashboard/API recheck; cumulative Uganda cases remained 19 and daily API rows for 2026-06-18, 2026-06-19, and 2026-06-20 reported zero cases.

No lab-confirmed case reported in Kasese District (Uganda) through the 2026-06-20 Uganda MoH dashboard/API recheck; cumulative Uganda cases remained 19 and daily API rows for 2026-06-18, 2026-06-19, and 2026-06-20 reported zero cases.

evidence.primary_publisher: DRC Ministry of Public Health / INSP / INRB
evidence.note: Reviewed SitRep #019 promotion dated 2026-06-02 includes Beni with 5 confirmed / 3 confirmed deaths, satisfying Beni-target calibration points inside their 20/21 May to 19/20 June windows. SitRep #035 continues to list Beni with 16 confirmed / 12 confirmed deaths.

No lab-confirmed case reported in Arua (Uganda) through the 2026-06-20 Uganda MoH dashboard/API recheck; cumulative Uganda cases remained 19 and daily API rows for 2026-06-18, 2026-06-19, and 2026-06-20 reported zero cases.

No lab-confirmed case reported in Nebbi District (Uganda) through the 2026-06-20 Uganda MoH dashboard/API recheck; cumulative Uganda cases remained 19 and daily API rows for 2026-06-18, 2026-06-19, and 2026-06-20 reported zero cases.

evidence.primary_publisher: Public calibration ledger resolution (2026-06-25), reviewed against ECDC and INSP SitRep promotions
evidence.note: No lab-confirmed BDBV case in Goma within the 2026-05-26 to 2026-06-25 window. The three public ledger rows registered 2026-05-26 for Ituri-source -> goma-cod (bunia, rwampara, mongbwalu) were all resolved NO on their 2026-06-25 resolution date under the public resolution protocol. Goma has since recorded a single confirmed case (1 confirmed at data date 2026-08-27, INRB SitRep 105), which post-dates the window and therefore does not resolve these points YES.
evidence.residual_uncertainty: The exact first-confirmation date for Goma is not established in this feed; the in-window determination rests on the dated public-ledger resolution of 2026-06-25 plus the fact that Goma's cumulative count stood at 1 as late as 2026-08-27. If a first-confirmation date inside the window is later published, this entry must be superseded by a new dated entry, not edited.

evidence.primary_publisher: Outbreak timeline, corroborated against WHO Disease Outbreak News 2026-DON613 (17 July 2026), which lists Tshopo among affected provinces (3 of 23 health zones)
evidence.note: Kisangani (Tshopo province) recorded its first confirmed BDBV case on 2026-06-30, inside the 2026-06-04 to 2026-07-04 window of the Block 4 kisangani-cod points. The associated death occurred 2026-06-27 in Bunia. By WHO DON613 (17 July 2026) Tshopo had 3 of 23 health zones affected; by the ECDC page updated 2026-08-31, Tshopo had 19 cases including 8 deaths across 7 of 23 health zones. LOVS carries makiso-kisangani-cod at 9 confirmed (data date 2026-08-27).
evidence.residual_uncertainty: The 2026-06-30 first-confirmation date is corroborated by two independent secondary sources but was not located in a primary WHO or INSP bulletin during this retrieval. Because 30 June sits four days inside a 30-day window, a primary-source confirmation of the date should be attached before this resolution is treated as settled.

evidence.primary_publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control
evidence.note: South Sudan has reported no confirmed BDBV case in this outbreak, so no case appeared in Yei within the 2026-06-04 to 2026-07-04 window. WHO Disease Outbreak News 2026-DON613 (17 July 2026) lists the affected countries as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, France and Germany, with no mention of South Sudan. The ECDC outbreak page, last updated 2026-08-31, lists DRC, Uganda, the United States, Germany and France, and records no South Sudan cases. South Sudan appears in both only in a preparedness and cross-border-surveillance context.

evidence.primary_publisher: Institut National de Sante Publique (INSP), DRC Ministry of Public Health: situation reports 47 (data 2026-06-30), 54 (2026-07-07), 57 (2026-07-10) and 58 (2026-07-11)
evidence.review: Dated, documented review: founder ruling of 2026-09-26. DRC targets resolve on promoted DRC MoH zone-attributed counts, as this file's purpose states. On that rule the 2026-06-04 block's two kisangani-cod points resolve NO, correcting the YES appended on 2026-09-01 from the superseded entry.
evidence.note: No laboratory-confirmed BDBV case was attributed to a Kisangani health zone between 2026-06-04 and 2026-07-04. INSP SitRep 47 (data 2026-06-30, published 2026-07-02) reports a sample that tested positive in Kisangani, taken from the body of a 24-year-old woman who died at PK 51, the Nia-Nia epicentre, and was moved clandestinely to Kisangani, and counts that case in Nia-Nia health zone, Ituri. SitRep 54 (2026-07-07) excludes two Kisangani positives on the RADIONE platform from the totals pending RT-PCR validation, one of them linked to Nia-Nia. SitRep 57 (2026-07-10) lists the Kisangani rows (Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo, Lubunga) as not counted because they are already included in Nia-Nia. SitRep 58 (2026-07-11) is the first to count the Kisangani health zones, after the window closed; it folds the Kisangani rows into the national total, so later tables place in Kisangani zones detections that earlier tables counted in Nia-Nia, possibly including the 29-30 June sample. This entry reads the first SitRep that counts a case in the zone, as the doctrine states. The public calibration record already dates Kisangani's first confirmation 2026-07-11 (bdbv-2026-cal-019). The superseded entry's 2026-06-30 date came from a secondary source, and its place of death (Bunia) is not supported by INSP.
